docket.challenge_claim: Three defects: the collection-scope rubric is folded into a single-nation oracle without the rubric-as-its-own-unit rival ever being tested; the address at Jer.46.11 is called the vision's first direct address although second-person imperatives already stand at 46:3 and 46:9; and the hedge withholding a count at 46:10 is attached to the bare adonai token rather than to the prefixed form actually quoted.
docket.grounds: All three verify on bytes. Scope first: oshb:Jer.46.1 (byte) closes on עַל הַגּוֹיִֽם, plural and naming no nation, while oshb:Jer.46.2 (byte) opens לְמִצְרַ֗יִם, lamed-scoped to one. The row states that scope difference in its own prose and then carries the span to Jer.46.12, and the rival it does test is a cut after both header verses on the prose-to-poetry shift - a different seam from the one its own scope sentence raises. That rival is live under the ruled granularity, since a lamed-initial nation header is itself a tier-1 onset, and the book's opening title stands as its own superscription-typed unit at Jer.1.1-Jer.1.3; leaving it unengaged is the defect, and any actual respan is a proposal, not a finding. Second: oshb:Jer.46.3 (byte) opens עִרְכ֤וּ מָגֵן֙ וְצִנָּ֔ה and oshb:Jer.46.9 (byte) opens עֲל֤וּ הַסּוּסִים֙, plural imperatives rendered as commands in both witnesses, and the row's own prose calls them imperatives addressed to unnamed combatants and a summons to the allied troops. Those are direct addresses; what is new at oshb:Jer.46.11 (byte) is the named vocative בְּתוּלַ֖ת בַּת מִצְרָ֑יִם, so the defensible claim is first named vocative, and a first-claim of any kind carries a digit-bearing sweep naming object and unit. Third: the form quoted at oshb:Jer.46.10 (byte) is לַאדֹנָ֧י יְהוִ֣ה צְבָא֗וֹת, the lamed-prefixed title stack - its own token object, byte-attested at two verses in the OAN block and invisible to a bare-token sweep. The hedge withholds a count on the ground that the bare skeleton token's point-aware split is unverified here, which is a different object; the caution is real but misfiled, and the count it declines is in fact available for the object actually quoted.
docket.remedy: strongest_rejected_alternative: engage the rival this row's own scope sentence raises - a cut at the oshb:Jer.46.1 / oshb:Jer.46.2 seam leaving the collection-scope rubric its own unit - and decide it on stated grounds; the rival now in the field is a different seam. Author work is to state and decide the rival in that field; moving the seam is a boundary proposal for owner adoption, never author work. boundary_rationale at oshb:Jer.46.11: replace 'The vision's first direct address' with the first named vocative, or keep a first-claim only with an adjacent digit-bearing sweep naming its object and unit. boundary_rationale at oshb:Jer.46.10: re-attach the hedge to the lamed-prefixed title stack actually quoted, or cite that object's own byte-attested site count instead of withholding one. Test: each cure must be re-derivable from the cited verse's own bytes for the object it names - the tests that killed the originals are reading oshb:Jer.46.3 and oshb:Jer.46.9 for imperatives before calling oshb:Jer.46.11 a first, and reading the oshb:Jer.46.10 form for its prefix before naming the sweep object.

current_row.boundary_rationale: A setumah closes oshb:Jer.45.5 in the parashah inventory (WLC, single-witness; tier-3 weak corroboration under the Prophets addendum). That mark falls immediately before this unit's own opening on the nations-rubric that stands over the whole collection, אֲשֶׁ֨ר הָיָ֧ה דְבַר יְהוָ֛ה אֶל יִרְמְיָ֥הוּ הַנָּבִ֖יא עַל הַגּוֹיִֽם (oshb:Jer.46.1, byte), matching “Yahweh’s word which came to Jeremiah the prophet concerning the nations.” (web:Jer.46.1) — one of only four verses in the book carrying this exact asher-hayah debar-YHWH el-Yirmeyahu shape (sweep: 4 verses), naming Jeremiah before naming any single nation. Egypt's own header follows at once with its date folded inside the same verse, לְמִצְרַ֗יִם עַל חֵ֨יל פַּרְעֹ֤ה נְכוֹ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ מִצְרַ֔יִם אֲשֶׁר הָיָ֥ה עַל נְהַר פְּרָ֖ת בְּכַרְכְּמִ֑שׁ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הִכָּ֗ה נְבֽוּכַדְרֶאצַּר֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ בָּבֶ֔ל בִּשְׁנַת֙ הָֽרְבִיעִ֔ית לִיהוֹיָקִ֥ים בֶּן יֹאשִׁיָּ֖הוּ מֶ֥לֶךְ יְהוּדָֽה (oshb:Jer.46.2, byte), matching “Of Egypt: concerning the army of Pharaoh Necoh king of Egypt, which was by the river Euphrates in Carchemish, which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon struck in the fourth year of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah, king of Judah.” (web:Jer.46.2) — Pharaoh Necoh, the Euphrates, Carchemish, and Nebuchadnezzar (spelled here נְבֽוּכַדְרֶאצַּר֙, the resh-family form) are all named before the battle-vision itself begins, and the fourth-year date sits header-internal rather than verse-initial. The battle-summons opens directly on the next verse with no intervening narration, עִרְכ֤וּ מָגֵן֙ וְצִנָּ֔ה וּגְשׁ֖וּ לַמִּלְחָמָֽה (oshb:Jer.46.3, byte), matching “Prepare the buckler and shield, and draw near to battle!” (web:Jer.46.3), continuing אִסְר֣וּ הַסּוּסִ֗ים וַֽעֲלוּ֙ הַפָּ֣רָשִׁ֔ים וְהִֽתְיַצְּב֖וּ בְּכ֥וֹבָעִ֑ים מִרְקוּ֙ הָֽרְמָחִ֔ים לִבְשׁ֖וּ הַסִּרְיֹנֹֽת (oshb:Jer.46.4, byte), matching “Harness the horses, and get up, you horsemen, and stand up with your helmets. Polish the spears, put on the coats of mail.” (web:Jer.46.4) — imperatives addressed to unnamed combatants, not yet a named vocative. Shock at the rout follows, מַדּ֣וּעַ רָאִ֗יתִי הֵ֣מָּה חַתִּים֮ נְסֹגִ֣ים אָחוֹר֒ וְגִבּוֹרֵיהֶ֣ם יֻכַּ֔תּוּ וּמָנ֥וֹס נָ֖סוּ וְלֹ֣א הִפְנ֑וּ מָג֥וֹר מִסָּבִ֖יב נְאֻם יְהוָֽה (oshb:Jer.46.5, byte), matching “Why have I seen it? They are dismayed and are turned backward. Their mighty ones are beaten down, have fled in haste, and don’t look back. Terror is on every side," says Yahweh.” (web:Jer.46.5); the verse closes on neum-YHWH, but no fresh tier-1 onset follows it at the next verse, so the formula corroborates rather than closes a unit here, and the flight continues without a break, אַל יָנ֣וּס הַקַּ֔ל וְאַל יִמָּלֵ֖ט הַגִּבּ֑וֹר צָפ֨וֹנָה֙ עַל יַ֣ד נְהַר פְּרָ֔ת כָּשְׁל֖וּ וְנָפָֽלוּ (oshb:Jer.46.6, byte), matching “Don’t let the swift flee away, nor the mighty man escape. In the north by the river Euphrates they have stumbled and fallen.” (web:Jer.46.6). A rhetorical question turns the description toward an extended Nile-simile, מִי זֶ֖ה כַּיְאֹ֣ר יַֽעֲלֶ֑ה כַּנְּהָר֕וֹת יִֽתְגָּעֲשׁ֖וּ מֵימָֽיו (oshb:Jer.46.7, byte), matching “Who is this who rises up like the Nile, like rivers whose waters surge?” (web:Jer.46.7), and Egypt's own boast is quoted inside the same figure, מִצְרַ֨יִם֙ כַּיְאֹ֣ר יַֽעֲלֶ֔ה וְכַנְּהָר֖וֹת יִתְגֹּ֣עֲשׁוּ מָ֑יִם וַיֹּ֗אמֶר אַֽעֲלֶה֙ אֲכַסֶּה אֶ֔רֶץ אֹבִ֥ידָה עִ֖יר וְיֹ֥שְׁבֵי בָֽהּ (oshb:Jer.46.8, byte), matching “Egypt rises up like the Nile, like rivers whose waters surge. He says, ‘I will rise up. I will cover the earth. I will destroy cities and its inhabitants.’” (web:Jer.46.8). A summons to the allied troops follows, עֲל֤וּ הַסּוּסִים֙ וְהִתְהֹלְל֣וּ הָרֶ֔כֶב וְיֵצְא֖וּ הַגִּבּוֹרִ֑ים כּ֤וּשׁ וּפוּט֙ תֹּפְשֵׂ֣י מָגֵ֔ן וְלוּדִ֕ים תֹּפְשֵׂ֖י דֹּ֥רְכֵי קָֽשֶׁת (oshb:Jer.46.9, byte), matching “Go up, you horses! Rage, you chariots! Let the mighty men go out: Cush and Put, who handle the shield; and the Ludim, who handle and bend the bow.” (web:Jer.46.9), and the scene is given its theological frame, וְֽהַיּ֨וֹם הַה֜וּא לַאדֹנָ֧י יְהוִ֣ה צְבָא֗וֹת י֤וֹם נְקָמָה֙ לְהִנָּקֵ֣ם מִצָּרָ֔יו וְאָכְלָ֥ה חֶ֨רֶב֙ וְשָׂ֣בְעָ֔ה וְרָוְתָ֖ה מִדָּמָ֑ם כִּ֣י זֶ֠בַח לַאדֹנָ֨י יְהוִ֧ה צְבָא֛וֹת בְּאֶ֥רֶץ צָפ֖וֹן אֶל נְהַר פְּרָֽת (oshb:Jer.46.10, byte), matching “For that day is of the Lord, Yahweh of Armies, a day of vengeance, that he may avenge himself of his adversaries. The sword will devour and be satiated, and will drink its fill of their blood; for the Lord, Yahweh of Armies, has a sacrifice in the north country by the river Euphrates.” (web:Jer.46.10) — the construction לַאדֹנָ֧י יְהוִ֣ה צְבָא֗וֹת is quoted here at the byte tier without a book-wide site count, since the adonai-skeleton token's point-aware split between the divine title and the courtly adoni address is not independently re-verified in this row. The vision's first direct address falls next, עֲלִ֤י גִלְעָד֙ וּקְחִ֣י צֳרִ֔י בְּתוּלַ֖ת בַּת מִצְרָ֑יִם לַשָּׁוְא֙ הרביתי הִרְבֵּ֣ית רְפֻא֔וֹת תְּעָלָ֖ה אֵ֥ין לָֽךְ (oshb:Jer.46.11, byte), matching “Go up into Gilead, and take balm, virgin daughter of Egypt. You use many medicines in vain. There is no healing for you.” (web:Jer.46.11) — direct address to Egypt personified as a virgin daughter, continuing the same battle-vision rather than opening a new one, and the verse itself carries a ketiv/qere pair, הרביתי written against הִרְבֵּ֣ית read (single-witness). The unit closes on a report of shared disgrace, שָׁמְע֤וּ גוֹיִם֙ קְלוֹנֵ֔ךְ וְצִוְחָתֵ֖ךְ מָלְאָ֣ה הָאָ֑רֶץ כִּֽי גִבּ֤וֹר בְּגִבּוֹר֙ כָּשָׁ֔לוּ יַחְדָּ֖יו נָפְל֥וּ שְׁנֵיהֶֽם (oshb:Jer.46.12, byte), matching “The nations have heard of your shame, and the earth is full of your cry; for the mighty man has stumbled against the mighty, they both fall together.” (web:Jer.46.12), echoing back to verse 6's own flight-language with its own closing image of mutual collapse. oshb:Jer.46.12 itself carries a closing petuchah in the marked-verse layer (WLC-sourced, single witness only, weak in the Prophets by owner ruling). A differently-shaped header opens the next verse, הַדָּבָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ הַנָּבִ֑יא לָב֗וֹא נְבֽוּכַדְרֶאצַּר֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ בָּבֶ֔ל לְהַכּ֖וֹת אֶת אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם (oshb:Jer.46.13, byte), matching “The word that Yahweh spoke to Jeremiah the prophet, how that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon should come and strike the land of Egypt:” (web:Jer.46.13), and this row stops short of that fresh onset.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting immediately after the header, on the strength of the shift from prose superscription to imperative battle-poetry, was considered and rejected: no divine-speech-frame, woe, or direct address to a named party intervenes before the address to Egypt personified as a virgin daughter, and that address continues the same Carchemish vision through its own close rather than opening an independent scene.

current_row.device_notes: The header-internal date argues only the byte-attested fourth year of Jehoiakim, not any external calendar; Nebuchadnezzar's name is spelled here in the dominant resh-family form, distinct from the nun-family spelling clustered in chapters 27-29.

docket.challenge_claim: The sole ground given for rejecting the strongest rival - that the heading carries no content of its own once split from the proclamation it frames - is false about Jer.46.13; the class generalization backing it carries no sweep digit and is contradicted at three sites of the eleven-verse header list; and the English run for 46:18 is left without its curly delimiter.
docket.grounds: The decisive half is upheld and the middle half needs correcting on both framing and digit. Upheld: oshb:Jer.46.13 (byte) carries its own topic clause, לָב֗וֹא נְבֽוּכַדְרֶאצַּר֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ בָּבֶ֔ל לְהַכּ֖וֹת אֶת אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם - Nebuchadnezzar's coming to strike the land of Egypt - which is content, and is what makes the verse a topical header at all; the row quotes that very clause in its own boundary prose and then rejects the rival on the ground that the verse has no content of its own. Whatever decides that rival, this ground cannot. Correction: the class claim is that the book's other prose headers open onto their first movement rather than standing as isolated citations, and a header verse that is itself content-free and hands the movement to the next verse is not a counter-instance to that reading, so 'contradicted' overstates. What is true, and is the residual defect, is that the claim is an undigited class generalization and that the class does not behave uniformly in the respect invoked: of the eleven verses carrying the hadavar-asher-hayah header shape, four are content-free - oshb:Jer.7.1, oshb:Jer.11.1, oshb:Jer.18.1 and oshb:Jer.30.1, byte-identical eight-token headers reading הַדָּבָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָיָ֣ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ מֵאֵ֥ת יְהוָ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר - and seven carry topic material. Four, not three; oshb:Jer.18.1 belongs in the count object, and a digit that names the wrong extension is itself a defect. The declared heuristic-false-positive disposition on this field's universal-claim flags does not survive: those flags land on this ground and on this generalization, and both are defects. The third item verifies in substance: the staged folded text of web:Jer.46.18 opens its second run with a curly double quote and the row's rendering substitutes a straight one, leaving that run undelimited; the run is otherwise character-for-character the staged text, so the defect is exactly the substitution, not a paraphrase.
docket.remedy: strongest_rejected_alternative: strike the ground that the heading carries no content of its own - oshb:Jer.46.13's own topic clause refutes it - and decide the rival on a ground the bytes support, or re-decide it. Same field: either drop the class generalization about the book's other prose headers or give it a digit-bearing sweep naming object and unit; on bytes the eleven-verse header class splits four content-free against seven content-bearing, so no uniform pattern may be asserted bare. boundary_rationale, the web:Jer.46.18 run: restore the curly opening the staged folded text carries on the second run, so the run is delimited and character-exact against that text. Test: the replacement ground must survive being read against oshb:Jer.46.13's own bytes - that reading killed the original - and every WEB run in the field must pass a character-for-character comparison with the staged folded text, run by run rather than at the one cited site.

current_row.boundary_rationale: The parashah inventory marks oshb:Jer.46.12 with a petuchah (WLC single witness; the Prophets addendum holds this tier-3 and never a driver). That mark falls immediately before this unit's own fresh word-event heading, הַדָּבָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ הַנָּבִ֑יא לָב֗וֹא נְבֽוּכַדְרֶאצַּר֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ בָּבֶ֔ל לְהַכּ֖וֹת אֶת אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם (oshb:Jer.46.13, byte), matching “The word that Yahweh spoke to Jeremiah the prophet, how that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon should come and strike the land of Egypt:” (web:Jer.46.13) — the shape here is built on the verb דִּבֶּ֣ר ("spoke") rather than the verb hayah ("came/was") that underlies all three of the book's canonical word-event shapes, so it is disclosed as its own header device rather than folded into any of them. The heading opens directly onto a fresh summons to proclaim, הַגִּ֤ידוּ בְמִצְרַ֨יִם֙ וְהַשְׁמִ֣יעוּ בְמִגְדּ֔וֹל וְהַשְׁמִ֥יעוּ בְנֹ֖ף וּבְתַחְפַּנְחֵ֑ס אִמְר֗וּ הִתְיַצֵּב֙ וְהָכֵ֣ן לָ֔ךְ כִּֽי אָכְלָ֥ה חֶ֖רֶב סְבִיבֶֽיךָ (oshb:Jer.46.14, byte), matching “Declare in Egypt, publish in Migdol, and publish in Memphis and in Tahpanhes; say, ‘Stand up, and prepare, for the sword has devoured around you.’” (web:Jer.46.14) — imperatives addressed to the frontier garrison towns rather than to Egypt as a single named addressee. A rhetorical question follows without any new frame, מַדּ֖וּעַ נִסְחַ֣ף אַבִּירֶ֑יךָ לֹ֣א עָמַ֔ד כִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה הֲדָפֽוֹ (oshb:Jer.46.15, byte), matching “Why are your strong ones swept away? They didn’t stand, because Yahweh pushed them.” (web:Jer.46.15), and the mercenaries' own flight is reported in their own quoted words, הִרְבָּ֖ה כּוֹשֵׁ֑ל גַּם נָפַ֞ל אִ֣ישׁ אֶל רֵעֵ֗הוּ וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ ק֣וּמָה וְנָשֻׁ֣בָה אֶל עַמֵּ֗נוּ וְאֶל אֶ֨רֶץ֙ מֽוֹלַדְתֵּ֔נוּ מִפְּנֵ֖י חֶ֥רֶב הַיּוֹנָֽה (oshb:Jer.46.16, byte), matching “He made many to stumble. Yes, they fell on one another. They said, ‘Arise! Let’s go again to our own people, and to the land of our birth, from the oppressing sword.’” (web:Jer.46.16) — this verse itself carries a paseq (single-witness, seg layer, count-only). The crowd's mockery of Pharaoh is quoted next, קָרְא֖וּ שָׁ֑ם פַּרְעֹ֤ה מֶֽלֶךְ מִצְרַ֨יִם֙ שָׁא֔וֹן הֶעֱבִ֖יר הַמּוֹעֵֽד (oshb:Jer.46.17, byte), matching “They cried there, ‘Pharaoh king of Egypt is but a noise; he has let the appointed time pass by.’” (web:Jer.46.17), and the unit closes on a divine oath, חַי אָ֨נִי֙ נְאֻם הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁמ֑וֹ כִּ֚י כְּתָב֣וֹר בֶּֽהָרִ֔ים וּכְכַרְמֶ֖ל בַּיָּ֥ם יָבֽוֹא (oshb:Jer.46.18, byte), matching “As I live,” says the King, whose name is Yahweh of Armies, "surely like Tabor among the mountains, and like Carmel by the sea, so he will come. (web:Jer.46.18) — the melekh-signature נְאֻם הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁמ֑וֹ, attributing the oath to the King whose name is Yahweh of Armies, names the oath's own speaker mid-verse rather than trailing it as a closing tag; it is one of only three sites of this exact construction in the book (sweep: 3 verses). The next verse opens on a fresh direct address, כְּלֵ֤י גוֹלָה֙ עֲשִׂ֣י לָ֔ךְ יוֹשֶׁ֖בֶת בַּת מִצְרָ֑יִם כִּֽי נֹף֙ לְשַׁמָּ֣ה תִֽהְיֶ֔ה וְנִצְּתָ֖ה מֵאֵ֥ין יוֹשֵֽׁב (oshb:Jer.46.19, byte), matching “You daughter who dwells in Egypt, furnish yourself to go into captivity; for Memphis will become a desolation, and will be burned up, without inhabitant.” (web:Jer.46.19), and this row stops at the oath that precedes it.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating verse 13 as opening its own row alone, separate from the summons it introduces, was considered and rejected: the heading carries no content of its own once split from the proclamation it frames, matching the pattern by which the book's other prose headers open directly onto their first movement rather than standing as an isolated citation.

docket.grounds: The substance is upheld with its framing corrected: the bracket is real at the construct level and cannot bear the weight the row puts on it. A token-bound skeleton sweep of the construct returns exactly three verses, all in this chapter - oshb:Jer.46.11, oshb:Jer.46.19, oshb:Jer.46.24 (sweep: 3 verses, skeleton tier) - so 'overstated' is right where 'absent' would not be. The opening edge at oshb:Jer.46.19 (byte) is a second-person address, עֲשִׂ֣י לָ֔ךְ with the vocative יוֹשֶׁ֖בֶת בַּת מִצְרָ֑יִם; the closing edge at oshb:Jer.46.24 (byte) reads הֹבִ֖ישָׁה בַּת מִצְרָ֑יִם נִתְּנָ֖ה, third-person throughout. What returns at the close is therefore the construct, not the address, and the device note's gloss of both edges as one dwelling daughter fits only the opening verse - the participle stands at oshb:Jer.46.19 and nowhere at the close, so gloss extent overruns splice extent there. The third occurrence is the material one: oshb:Jer.46.11 (byte) carries the same construct under the same second-person address, עֲלִ֤י גִלְעָד֙ וּקְחִ֣י with בְּתוּלַ֖ת בַּת מִצְרָ֑יִם, eight verses earlier and outside this span, disclosed nowhere in the row and absent from its evidence refs. A byte-true device straddling a row's own seams argues continuity against the row unless disclosed, and this one runs across two of them. The front seam itself survives - the address at oshb:Jer.46.19 is genuinely fresh against the oath closing before it, and the tier-3 mark there is correctly held to corroboration - but the span-bounding force claimed for the bracket does not.
docket.remedy: device_notes and the closing sentence of boundary_rationale: re-cut the framing claim to what the bytes bracket - the bat-Mitsrayim construct, carrying its digit and object (sweep: 3 verses, skeleton tier) - and state that the opening edge is a second-person address while the closing edge is third-person, so the bracket is on the figure and not on the address; drop the participle from the gloss of the closing edge, which does not carry it. A form-class label is a byte-checkable claim under the same discipline as a digit, and this one is asserted twice, in the boundary prose and again in the device note, with the unit carried at high confidence and no morphology layer in the substrate to have suggested otherwise. Low is right: nothing in the seam turns on the label. The rest verifies - the header at oshb:Jer.47.1 is one of the four verses carrying that shape, the divine-speech formula at oshb:Jer.47.2 sets this frame rather than changing an established one, the marks at oshb:Jer.47.1 and oshb:Jer.47.5 stand at their claimed type with the preceding mark at oshb:Jer.46.28 cited correctly (single-witness, tier-3 weak in the Prophets), the single paseq at oshb:Jer.47.2 is cited count-only, and no ketiv/qere note falls in the span.
